title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on vitamin D status and physical performance in football players: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Low vitamin D status is frequently reported among athletes, but whether vitamin D supplementation improves physical performance in football players remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentration, jump performance, sprint performance, aerobic capacity, and muscular performance in association football and futsal players.

title: Genomic and probiotic characterization of newly isolated Akkermansia strains from camel and horse feces in alleviating obesity and metabolic dysregulation.
abstract: Accumulating evidence points to Akkermansia muciniphila as a promising candidate to improve obesity-associated metabolic disorders. However, studies on the isolation, identification, and functional validation of Akkermansia strains from the intestines of animals occupying specialized ecological niches (such as camel and horse) remain limited. In this study, we isolated an Akkermansia muciniphila strain Muc_T9 and an Akkermansia massiliensis strain Mas_DA from camel and horse feces, respectively....

title: [Investigation of the Antagonistic Effects and Cytokine, Chemokine and TLR4 Profiles of Human-Derived Lactic Acid Bacteria Co-cultured with Escherichia coli Serotypes on the Caco-2 Colon Cell Line].
abstract: The antagonistic ability of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) is an important factor in the evaluation of probiotics. Therefore, the colonization ability and persistence of probiotics in the gastrointestinal tract is one of the most important criteria in preventing the adhesion of pathogenic bacteria to epithelial cells to reduce pathogen-associated diseases. This study aimed to investigate the interaction of LAB, whose probiotic properties were determined in previous studies, with Escherichia coli str...

title: The impact of probiotics or synbiotics on individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune condition characterized by insulin deficiency. Probiotics and synbiotics are believed to impact glycemic control. This study aims to evaluate their effects on individuals with T1DM.

title: Navigating Supplement Use in Solid Tumor Oncology: A Comprehensive Review of Clinical, Regulatory, and Safety Considerations.
abstract: Between 50 and 85% of patients with solid tumors use dietary supplements following cancer diagnosis, commonly with the intent to boost immune function, alleviate treatment-related toxicities, and improve outcomes. Despite this high prevalence, supplement use is frequently undisclosed to treating oncologists, constraining clinicians' ability to identify clinically meaningful drug-supplement interactions and provide evidence-based counseling. This review synthesizes available evidence on the effic...

title: Effects of Lactobacillus crispatus-Containing Probiotics and Metformin on Insulin Resistance, Inflammation, and Gut Microbiome in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Protocol for an Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects 9% to 12% of reproductive-age women worldwide, with higher prevalence reported in India. Its pathophysiology involves insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, and chronic low-grade inflammation, increasingly linked to gut dysbiosis and lipopolysaccharide-driven toll-like receptor 4 signaling. Elevated calprotectin and suppressed acylated ghrelin (AGH) reflect this inflammatory-metabolic disruption. While metformin remains standard therapy, it does not addres...

title: The impact of nutrition on glaucoma progression: evidence from systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to determine if nutritional interventions have an impact on glaucoma progression. The clinical question being answered is whether nutritional supplementation compared to baseline values has an impact on measures of glaucoma progression, i.e., intraocular pressure (IOP), visual field mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness.

title: A Lactobacillus acidophilus LA15-Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Bi66 consortium alleviates loperamide-induced constipation by coordinating gut microbiota remodeling, mucosal barrier repair, and aquaporin-mediated water transport.
abstract: Functional constipation is increasingly recognized as a microbiota-associated disorder involving impaired motility, low-grade inflammation, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and abnormal intestinal water transport. This study evaluated whether a defined probiotic consortium composed of Lactobacillus acidophilus LA15 and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Bi66 (AB consortium; 1:1) could alleviate loperamide-induced constipation and clarified its microbiota-metabolite-barrier mechanism. Male KM ...

title: Complementary strategies to target residual immune activation and mucosal dysfunction in treated HIV: role of probiotics and pidotimod.
abstract: Alterations in the microbiota, loss of mucosal barrier integrity, and persistent immune activation are important determinants of susceptibility to infections and, in people with HIV receiving effective antiretroviral therapy, of non-AIDS comorbidities. This narrative mini-review examines two mechanistically distinct interventions within a shared translational hypothesis: strain-specific probiotics may act upstream by modifying the intestinal ecosystem and barrier function, whereas pidotimod may ...
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Weissella koreensis regulates mitochondrial protective genes and innate immune genes to enhance anti-bacterial immunity.
abstract: Probiotics are widely recognized for their ability to promote gut health, modulate immunity, and reduce oxidative stress. As an emerging probiotic within the genus Weissella, Weissella koreensis (WK) exhibits promising immunomodulatory potential. Recent evidence highlights its potential as a functional probiotic in combating obesity. However, its specific role in host immune regulation and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely undefined. In this study, we demonstrate that, compared ...

title: The association of dietary methionine, natural folate and folic acid supplementation with the risk of preterm birth during pregnancy: a case control study.
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association of dietary methionine, natural folate and folic acid supplementation with the risk of preterm birth during pregnancy and to assess the interaction between dietary methionine and folic acid.

title: Metabolic, enzymatic, and probiotic profiling of Lactococcus lactis LBM15: inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus biofilm and virulence genes, and GPR-based prediction.
abstract: This study characterized a Lactococcus lactis strain (LBM15) isolated from traditional yogurt and evaluated its probiotic, antimicrobial, and anti-biofilm attributes, along with its physiological robustness and safety-associated characteristics. The isolate was identified by 16S rRNA sequencing (99% similarity) and exhibited a carbohydrate utilization pattern typical of dairy L. lactis, including efficient fermentation of common hexoses and β-glucosides. Enzymatic profiling revealed high phospha...

title: Resistance training and protein supplementation in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer: a randomized feasibility trial.
abstract: Cancer cachexia is associated with reduced physical performance, quality of life, and survival in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer. Resistance training and protein supplementation have the potential to improve these outcomes. Whether an intervention comprising resistance training and protein supplementation is feasible during treatment for incurable gastroesophageal cancer is not known.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

title: Impact of carotenoids on body composition and adipokine hormones: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Carotenoids, a class of antioxidant phytochemicals, have been proposed to influence adiposity and metabolic regulation through modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and adipokine secretion. However, clinical evidence remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively evaluate the effects of carotenoid supplementation on anthropometric and adipokine parameters, including body weight, body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), hip circumference (HC...

title: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 ameliorates age-related intestinal hypomotility in older adults: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: The decay of smooth muscle contractility is a major trigger of aging-related intestinal hypomotility, which imposes a substantial healthcare burden. Despite this, effective targeted therapy for this condition remains unavailable. Here, we identified the probiotic Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 as a microbiota modulator that restores gut motility through the bile acid (BA)-mediated rescue of smooth muscle contractile function. In a randomized, double-blind clinical trial (ChiCTR2300...

title: Vitamin D Supplementation During COVID-19 Infection Is Associated With an Unfavorable Impact of Increased Total Number of Organ Systems Involved.
abstract: Introduction: COVID-19 is a systemic disease that affects multiple organ systems. We investigated the association between vitamin D supplementation and the number of organ systems involved in hospitalized patients with COVID-19.
journal: WMJ : official publication of the State Medical Society of Wisconsin

title: Engineered synbiotic microspheres enable system-level reprogramming of the gut-immune-vascular axis in chronic inflammatory vascular disease.
abstract: Chronic inflammatory vascular diseases are increasingly recognized as systemic disorders sustained by maladaptive cross-organ immunometabolic coupling, yet current therapeutic strategies remain largely lesion-centered and fail to address upstream drivers of disease persistence. Here, we identify the gut-immune-vascular axis as a system-level pathogenic unit that integrates gut microbial dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, metabolic imbalance, and vascular immune activation into a self-rei...

title: Opportunities and challenges for introduction of balanced energy protein supplementation through routine antenatal care.
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends balanced energy and protein (BEP) supplementation during pregnancy in contexts where prevalence of maternal underweight, defined as body mass index (BMI) < 18.5 kg/m2, is ≥ 20%. Evidence shows that BEP supplementation in underweight pregnant women reduces the risk of low birthweight, small for gestational age, and preterm birth. Yet little is known about how to introduce BEP through routine antenatal care (ANC). This paper explores challenges, oppor...

title: Effects of Probiotics on Migraine in Children and Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Increasing evidence highlights a link between migraine, a disabling neurological disorder, and the gut microbiome. Probiotics, supplements containing colony-forming units of beneficial microbes, may influence migraine via the gut microbiome. A systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials was completed, and findings were synthesized narratively to evaluate probiotics for migraine prevention.

title: Allobaculum stercoricanis and Its Postbiotics Alleviate Dextran Sulfate Sodium (DSS)-Induced Colitis through the Regulation of theTLR4/NF-κB Signaling Pathway.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disorder that has become a global public health concern. Postbiotics offer advantages in biosafety and reproducibility over probiotics. Here, we demonstrated that live Allobaculum stercoricanis (A. stercoricanis) and its two postbiotic preparations─inactivated bacterial cells (POST) and cell-free fermentation supernatant (CFS)─effectively alleviated dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice. Integrated gut microbiome and serum m...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Surface-functionalized Bifidobacterium bifidum alleviates Clostridioides difficile infection by coordinating host immune modulation and gut microbiota restoration☆.
abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a major ecological disruption of the gut ecosystem, characterized by loss of colonization resistance, persistent inflammatory feedback and incomplete microbial recovery. Meta-analysis of clinical cohorts identified Bifidobacterium depletion as a conserved feature of CDI-associated dysbiosis, suggesting that restoring this genus may promote recovery from CDI. Comparative in vitro assays identified B. bifidum as the most protective strain. This effect wa...

title: Psychobiotics: A Paradigm Shift in Dermatological Disorders.
abstract: Recent clinical studies have demonstrated an intricate bidirectional system in the gut-brain-skin axis. Here, the gut microbiome plays dual roles: it can act as a pathological factor while also serving as a potential therapeutic target in psychodermatology. Chronic skin conditions (CSCs) like acne vulgaris, atopic dermatitis, and psoriasis are some of the leading skin problems. Besides that, these conditions are not only associated with anxiety and depression but also result in a drastic decline...

title: Hierarchical microspheres responsive to pH and MMP-9 for site-specific probiotic delivery and oxidative stress mitigation.
abstract: Probiotic oral delivery is limited by gastrointestinal harshness and lack of inflammation-responsive release. This study presents a hierarchical hydrogel microsphere platform (LAB@SGT) assembled from food-derived components, with a photocrosslinked core derived from food-grade gelatin, featuring an ionically crosslinked sodium alginate shell and a tea polyphenol palmitate (TPP)-reinforced allyl-modified gelatin (GelAGE) core. title: Biotransformation of bioactive profiles and metabolomic remodeling of germinated brown rice milk fermented with probiotic Lactiplantibacillus plantarum.
abstract: This study aimed to isolate, molecularly characterize, and apply multifunctional probiotic lactic acid bacteria (LAB) from traditional Thai fermented sources (dough balls and Khao Mak) to formulate bioactively enriched fermented germinated brown rice milk (FGBRM) using indigenous rice cultivars (Maled Fai, Red Jasmine, and KDML105). title: Transforming red lentils into a gut-friendly food: Limosilactobacillus fermentum pro-227 fermentation degrades oligosaccharides and enhances prebiotic properties.
abstract: The flatulence factors in red lentils (Lens culinaris), such as raffinose and stachyose, may limit their consumption among individuals sensitive to gastrointestinal discomfort. This study screened Limosilactobacillus fermentum pro-227, a high α-galactosidase-producing strain from the feces of healthy and long-lived elderly people to ferment red lentils (LFRL), to ferment red lentils under optimized conditions (35 °C, solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:1, inoculum level of 3%) for 24 h. title: Randomized Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of a Supplement and Serum on Grey Hair.
abstract: Worldwide, 74% of men and women between the ages of 45 and 65 have some grey hair. Currently, there is no treatment that has been shown in a clinical trial to repigment or slow the development of grey hair. In this study, we investigated the efficacy of a topical and supplement regimen (To The Root® serum and Not Today Grey supplement (Two Lines Inc.). A total of 173 men and women aged 28 to 65 years, with 5–25% grey hair, completed the study. Participants were randomized to include at...
journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD

title: Central Centrifugal Cicatricial Alopecia and the Use of Xtressé Nutrient Supplement: A Case Series.
abstract: Central Centrifugal Cicatricial Alopecia (CCCA) is a form of scarring alopecia characterized by patches of permanent hair loss that manifests on the crown of the scalp, progressively spreading outward in a centrifugal pattern.1 This condition is predominantly observed in African American women. Treatment options for CCCA remain limited, with current treatments including topical and systemic corticosteroids and oral tetracyclines, with modest responses.1 We present 2 cases of CCCA treated with Xt...
journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD

title: Beyond live probiotics: bioactivities, mechanisms, and application perspectives of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus cell-free supernatants.
abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus is one of the most widely investigated probiotic species. Live preparations can modulate intestinal microbiota, support immune function, and ameliorate metabolic disorders. However, poor stability during processing and storage, low gastrointestinal survival, variable intestinal colonization, and potential risks in immunocompromised individuals limit the use of live preparations. Therefore, an increasing number of studies have focused on cell-free supernatant (CFS). S...

title: Nutraceutical and herbal interventions targeting inflammation and oxidative stress in PCOS-associated insulin resistance.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women of reproductive age. It is commonly associated with insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, chronic low-grade inflammation, and oxidative stress. These factors contribute to metabolic dysfunction and increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular complications. This narrative review critically evaluates the available evidence regarding nutraceutical and herbal interventions targeting ...

title: Effects of Vitamin D 3 Supplementation on Glycaemic Parameters and Insulin Sensitivity in Pre-diabetic Adults: A Prospective Controlled Interventional Study.
abstract: Pre-diabetes precedes type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and is characterised by impaired fasting glucose, impaired glucose tolerance or both. Vitamin D deficiency is prevalent in India and implicated in impaired glucose metabolism and insulin resistance, yet interventional data from Indian pre-diabetic populations remain limited.

title: The gut-microbiota-endometriosis axis: a review of immune regulation, microbial dysbiosis, host transcriptomics, probiotic intervention, and dietary influences.
abstract: Endometriosis is a persistent gynaecological disease state marked by development of endometrial-like tissue exterior to the uterus, which triggers pelvic discomfort, chronic inflammation, and fertility issues. Although it has been associated with hormonal imbalances and immune dysfunction, emerging research describes a major role for the microbiota in initiating and accelerating the disease. Disruptions in the gut microbiota have been associated with immune system activation and inflammatory sig...

title: Effect of postpartum probiotic supplementation on breastmilk composition and infant health: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Breast milk is the optimal infant nutrition, and its composition is influenced by maternal factors including supplement intake. This study aimed to investigate the effects of postpartum probiotic supplementation on breast milk composition and infant health outcomes.

title: Effects of dietary supplementation with Enterococcus faecalis JM263 on growth performance, antioxidant status, rumen microbiota and metabolism in yaks.
abstract: Yaks are vital to the ecology and economy of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau. The unique environmental conditions of this high-altitude region have shaped yaks, leading to significant differences in their evolution from other cattle species. From yak gut contents, we isolated Enterococcus faecalis JM263, a novel probiotic with strong fiber-degrading ability. To investigate the effects of E. faecalis JM263 on the growth performance, antioxidant capacity, rumen microbiome, and metabolites of captive ya...

title: Microbiome-directed therapies in oncology: from animal models to clinical implementation.
abstract: The gut microbiota is increasingly recognized as a key regulator of cancer development, antitumor immunity, treatment response, and therapy-related toxicity. Microbial dysbiosis contributes to chronic inflammation, impaired intestinal barrier function, and immune dysregulation, thereby influencing oncological outcomes. This review summarizes current evidence on probiotics and microbiome-directed interventions in oncology, from mechanistic studies to emerging clinical applications. We discuss int...

title: A multivariate PCA-based evaluation of betaine, vitamin C, and phytogenic (STRESS-BIOMax) - supplemented drinking water in broilers?
abstract: Physiological and metabolic disturbances can impair growth and oxidative balance in broilers. This study evaluated the effects of Stress-BioMax (SBM) supplementation in drinking water (0.00, 0.25, 0.50, and 1.00 mL/L) on growth performance, carcass traits, biochemical indices, oxidative status, and systemic physiological responses. SBM is a drinking-water additive containing betaine, vitamin C, and herbal extracts. Principal component analysis (PCA), quadratic regression, and segmented regressio...

title: Chickpea flour (Cicer arietinum L) improves viability of potentially probiotics Lactobacillus plantarum S180.7 and Lactobacillus plantarum SBR64.7 in milk-based formulations.
abstract: This study evaluated the effect of adding chickpea flour to milk-based formulations on physicochemical parameters, the survival, and viability of potentially probiotic microorganisms. Four formulations were prepared using skimmed milk (10%) and sucrose (10%), each containing Lactobacillus plantarum S180.7 (CF1) or L. plantarum SBR64.7 (CF2), with or without 4.5% chickpea flour (TF1 and TF2). Composition, physicochemical properties, total phenolic content, antioxidant activity, and bacterial viab...

title: Vitamins E and C supplementation reduces hepatic lipid peroxidation and steatosis in neonatal Yucatan piglets receiving prolonged parenteral nutrition.
abstract: Parenteral nutrition (PN) is essential in neonatal care for many infants born prematurely or with impaired gastrointestinal function. However, prolonged PN use is associated with complications such as PN-associated liver disease and intestinal atrophy, potentially related to oxidative stress. Commercial PN lipid emulsions with fish oil are used to counteract PN-associated liver damage but may also contribute to oxidative stress due to their high content of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids....

title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Effects of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on physical function and body composition in older adults: a narrative review.
abstract: Healthy aging is a priority for many individuals; however, a decline in physical function and poor body composition are common age-related changes that can cause the added years from rising life expectancy to be spent in poor health. Consequently, understanding the mechanisms involved in aging has become increasingly important, including the role of phospholipids (PLs) and how age-related changes in PL content may interfere with lipid metabolism and normal functioning of the musculoskeletal syst...
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Cinnamon supplementation in broiler and laying hen diets: benefits, mechanisms, supplementation doses, and limitations - a review.
abstract: Cinnamon and its derivatives (bark powder, essential oil, extract, and nanoparticles) were used as phytogenic feed additives (PFAs) in the modern poultry industry possibly due to their antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and gut-promoting properties. The present review pools recent studies on the effects of cinnamon supplementation on broiler and laying hen performance, focusing on growth performance, carcass and meat quality, egg production, egg quality, and hatchability. Cinnamon bi...

title: Probiotic Extracellular Vesicles: Bridging Lacticaseibacillus casei and the Intestinal Epithelium.
abstract: The mechanisms underlying the health benefits of probiotics remain incompletely understood. Among the proposed mediators, bacterial extracellular vesicles (EVs) have been proposed as mediators of interkingdom communication between probiotic bacteria and their hosts. In this study, we show that Lacticaseibacillus casei BL23 releases higher EV levels during late stationary phase, with a predominant population of ∼113 nm. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed the ultrastructural morphology o...

title: Safety Assessment of Spirulina Intake on Cytochrome P450 3A-Mediated Drug Metabolism: A Comprehensive Study from an In Vitro Study to a Human Clinical Trial.
abstract: Spirulina has been gaining increasing attention as a dietary supplement, yet its potential to induce food-drug interactions when taken alongside medications remains insufficiently understood. Inhibition of cytochrome P450 3A (CYP3A), a major drug-metabolizing enzyme, is of concern, as it may play a key role in adverse effect development. Therefore, we aimed to determine whether spirulina induces food-drug interactions through CYP3A inhibition. To assess the inhibitory effects of spirulina on CYP...
journal: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology

title: Region-Adapted Multi-Nutrient Supplementation in Chinese Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A 12-Week Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: Nutritional supplementation has produced inconsistent effects on autistic symptoms, and the evidence base is largely derived from Western populations. This study evaluated the preliminary efficacy and tolerability of a region-adapted multinutrient intervention in Chinese children with autism spectrum disorder. In this 12-wk pilot, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 50 children were assigned to receive either the intervention or a placebo. The primary endpoint was the change in t...
journal: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology

title: Lacticaseibacillus paracasei INIA P708: a safe human isolate with probiotic and technological potential.
abstract: Lacticaseibacillus paracasei INIA P708 was isolated from breast-fed infant feces. It stood out by its stable ropy phenotype, which could indicate exopolysaccharide (EPS) production and antimicrobial properties. Bearing in mind its potential use in the food chain, the objective of this work was to study L. paracasei INIA P708 potential probiotic traits, and technological and safety characteristics, in comparison to the commercial probiotic L. rhamnosus GG strain. A full genomic analysis was also ...

title: Exploration of glucose lowering ability of Moringa oleifera polysaccharide in simulated intestinal and liver environment: an integrated in vitro investigation of its prebiotic potential, intestinal transport, and hepatic insulin-resistance-related response.
abstract: Moringa oleifera leaf polysaccharide (MOLP) is a dietary fiber with hypoglycemic activity, but the relationships among its microbial fermentation, epithelial transport, and hepatic effects remain unclear. Here, an integrated in vitro platform comprising pooled human fecal fermentation, bifidobacterial monoculture assays, Caco-2 transepithelial transport, and insulin-resistant HepG2 cells was used to investigate a potential gut-liver axis mediated by MOLP. Compared with commercial larch arabinoga...

title: Unlocking the prebiotic potential of shiitake stipes insoluble dietary Fiber-bound Phenolics: Structural modulation, antioxidant release, and gut microbiota regulation via untargeted metabolomics.
abstract: Shiitake stipes, a major by-product of mushroom cultivation, are a rich source of insoluble dietary fiber (IDF) covalently bound to phenolic compounds. This study investigated the functional relationship between bound phenolics (BP) and IDF by comparing native BP-IDF with phenolics-removed IDF (RP-IDF). The removal of BP was associated with marked changes in fiber morphology and significantly reduced water/oil-holding capacities, swelling power and antioxidant activity, suggesting that BP may co...

title: Effects of Saccharomyces cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 and vitamin K2 on the gut microbiota of patients with osteoporosis and healthy controls using in vitro short-term colonic simulations.
abstract: The gut microbiome may be involved in bone health through the gut-bone axis. Saccharomyces cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 benefits gut health in patients with irritable bowel syndrome, which is more prevalent in women and may be associated with higher osteoporosis prevalence. We evaluated the effects of S. cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 ± vitamin K2 (K2) on the gut microbiota of patients with osteoporosis and healthy controls. Short-term in vitro colonic fermentations were performed using feces from healthy and...

title: Oat-grape probiotic beverage enriched with jambolan extract improves glycemic markers and pancreatic morphology in a rat model of type 2 diabetes.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disease accounting for approximately 90% of all diabetes cases worldwide, highlighting the need for effective prevention and management strategies. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of an oat-grape probiotic beverage enriched with 3% jambolan (Syzygium cumini) extract (PBA3) containing Lactobacillus acidophilus LA14 in Wistar rats with T2DM. Rats were randomized into four groups: healthy control (H), healthy treated with PBA3 (HB), di...

title: Bibliometric Analysis of Global Research Trends on Probiotic-Based Interventions for Postmenopausal Osteoporosis.
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) is a major skeletal disorder associated with increased fracture risk and substantial morbidity. Growing evidence links the gut microbiota with bone homeostasis, supporting investigation of probiotic-based interventions through immunomodulation, maintenance of intestinal barrier function, and production of short-chain fatty acids. Existing bibliometric studies have examined broader relationships between the gut microbiota, bone metabolism, and osteoporosis; the ...

title: Early post-weaning probiotic supplementation alters gut microbial community structure and predicted metabolic function in female juvenile mice.
abstract: To characterize the effects of early post-weaning multi-strain probiotic supplementation on gut microbiota composition, predicted metabolic function, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles in female juvenile mice at the pubertal window.
